cards.text: Short one, friend: fourteen verses from John, who calls himself the elder. He's writing to one man, Gaius, whom he calls beloved and says he loves in the truth. I've written longer notes on the back of a takeout menu!

cards.question: John opens by praying that Gaius will prosper and enjoy good health in every way. What does John say is already prospering?

cards.text: Some brothers came to John and testified about Gaius's devotion to the truth, and Gaius is still walking in it. How does John take the news? Like a man who just pulled a PERFECT batch out of the oven.

cards.question: John says he has no greater ___ than to hear that his children are walking in the truth.

cards.text: Then John tells Gaius he's faithful in what he's doing for the brothers. FAITHFUL, friend! I've had oven timers that couldn't make it through one batch.

cards.question: True or false: Gaius already knew these brothers well before he helped them.

cards.text: Those brothers testified to the church about Gaius's love, and friend, that beats any five-star review.

cards.question: What does John say Gaius will do well to do for these brothers?

answers.text: Send them on in a manner worthy of God
Keep them in his own home for good
Bring them before the elders in Jerusalem

cards.question: These brothers went out on behalf of the Name. John says they accepted ___ from the Gentiles.
True or false: John says that supporting men like these makes us fellow workers for the truth.

cards.text: Now the letter turns, friend. John says he wrote to the church about this, but a man named Diotrephes "will not accept our instruction."

cards.question: Diotrephes won't accept the instruction John sent to the church. John says Diotrephes loves to be ___.

cards.text: Loves to be first, like the dead batteries I shared a drawer with, arguing ALL DAY over who had the most charge left. And John says if he comes, he'll call attention to Diotrephes's malicious slander against them.

cards.question: Slander isn't enough for Diotrephes. What does he refuse to do for the brothers?
True or false: Diotrephes lets others in the church welcome the brothers if they want to.
John turns back to Gaius: "Beloved, do not imitate what is evil, but what is good." The one who does good is of God. What does John say about the one who does evil?

answers.text: He has not heard the Word

cards.text: Then John brings up a new name: Demetrius. Different man, VERY different report.

cards.question: Demetrius has a good testimony from everyone, and from the truth itself. True or false: John refuses to add his own testimony for Demetrius.

cards.text: John's got many things left to write, but he'd rather skip the pen and ink and see Gaius soon, face to face. Friend, John is NOT a group chat guy.

cards.question: John signs off wishing Gaius peace and sending greetings from the friends with him. What does he ask Gaius to do for the friends where Gaius is?

answers.text: Greet each of them by name
Send them all to visit John
